title: Creme Caramel
subtitle: Set vanilla custard with a bittersweet caramel sauce
excerpt: A silky, smooth baked custard that unmoulds to reveal a gleaming pool of dark caramel. One of the most elegant and forgiving of all French desserts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Creme caramel (or flan in Spanish and Latin American cooking) is a baked custard dessert in which a caramel is poured into ramekins before the custard, so that when the cold dessert is unmoulded, the caramel forms a sauce over the top. The dish is found across France, Spain, Portugal, and their former territories. The custard is a simple mixture of whole eggs, egg yolks, sugar, and whole milk (sometimes enriched with cream), flavoured with vanilla and cooked in a bain-marie (water bath) in the oven. The water bath prevents the oven heat from curdling the outside of the custard before the centre sets. The caramel should be taken to a deep amber: if it is too pale it will be sweet without bitterness; if taken too far it will be bitter without sweetness. A well-made creme caramel should tremble when gently shaken.

recipeTools.notes: A deep roasting tin to use as a water bath (bain-marie).

content.text: The caramel is made without stirring: swirl the pan but do not stir, as stirring can cause crystallisation. Take the caramel to a deep amber and pour immediately into the ramekins before it sets. The custard mixture should be strained through a sieve to remove any threads of cooked egg white that might form lumps. Bake in a water bath just deep enough to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins. The custard is done when it is set around the edges but still trembles in the centre.

items.preparation: 100 g for the caramel, 100 g for the custard

content.text: Make the caramel: put 100 g of the sugar in a heavy saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water. Cook over medium-high heat, swirling the pan occasionally, until the sugar melts and turns a deep amber. Pour immediately into 6 ramekins, tilting each to coat the base. Work fast.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Warm the milk and cream together in a saucepan with the vanilla until almost simmering. Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, and remaining 100 g of sugar together until combined. Pour the warm milk mixture over the egg mixture in a steady stream, whisking constantly. Strain through a sieve.

Pour the custard into the ramekins. Place the ramekins in a deep roasting tin. Pour boiling water around them to come halfway up the sides. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until set at the edges and still trembling in the centre. Remove from the water bath and cool. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
To unmould, run a thin knife around the edge of each ramekin, place a plate over the top, and invert in one firm motion. Lift the ramekin off. The caramel will pool around the custard.
